New machine. Its objects are: tibedas, fatudok, badili, bitolos, bineko, denirer.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: tibedas, fatudok, badili
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Nothing lit for the first three. Since I don't yet know whether the machine needs one nexiom or both to light up, I'll test the other three objects to compare.

TEST: bitolos, bineko, denirer
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit on its own, yet the two nexioms must be somewhere among the six. So one nexiom alone is not enough to light the machine. The likeliest rule is that it lights only when both nexioms are present. That would put one nexiom in {tibedas, fatudok, badili} and one in {bitolos, bineko, denirer}, giving 9 possible pairs.

I'll test two objects from each group. If it lights, 4 pairs remain, and my last 2 tests can always settle those. If it doesn't, 5 pairs remain, and I may not be able to rule them all out.

TEST: tibedas, fatudok, bitolos, bineko
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Assuming the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, the first two results mean one nexiom is in {tibedas, fatudok, badili} and the other is in {bitolos, bineko, denirer}. The last test then rules out any pair made from tibedas or fatudok with bitolos or bineko. Five pairs remain:
- badili + bitolos
- badili + bineko
- badili + denirer
- tibedas + denirer
- fatudok + denirer

Two yes/no tests can only tell apart four outcomes, so I can't guarantee an answer. I'll split the pairs 3/2 to give the best chance. This test contains badili+bitolos, badili+denirer and tibedas+denirer. If it doesn't light, only two pairs are left, and my last test can tell them apart.

TEST: badili, bitolos, denirer, tibedas
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

If the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, three pairs fit all the results so far:
- badili + bitolos
- badili + denirer
- tibedas + denirer

One yes/no test can't tell three pairs apart, so I can't be sure of the answer. This test checks one pair directly. If it lights, the answer is badili + denirer. If it doesn't, I'll have to guess between the other two.

TEST: badili, denirer
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The machine lit up with just badili and denirer on it. Under my working rule that it lights only when both nexioms are present, that pair must be the answer. It also fits every earlier result: neither half had both, test 3 had neither, and test 4 had both.

This rests on that rule, which I inferred rather than confirmed. The first two tests did show that one nexiom alone isn't enough, which makes the rule very likely.

ANSWER: nexioms = badili, denirer
One last question. If only badili were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up. In my very first test, badili was on the machine with tibedas and fatudok, and nothing happened. If badili and denirer are the nexioms, tibedas and fatudok are not, and non-nexioms never affect the machine. So that test was effectively badili on its own, and it did not light. This conclusion comes straight from that observation and doesn't depend on my assumed rule.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: vuguguk, telidu, vamepek, kaguku, lareges, buzekur.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow things down.

TEST: vuguguk, telidu, vamepek
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group of three lit up, so at least one nexiom is probably in it, though I don't yet know the machine's rule. Next I'll test the other three to see whether both nexioms are in the first group or split between the groups.

TEST: kaguku, lareges, buzekur
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The second group did not light up. Two rules for the machine fit both results:
- **Any nexiom lights it:** then both nexioms must be in the first group, since the second group contains none.
- **It needs both nexioms:** then both must again be in the first group, because that is the only group that lit.

So the nexioms are very likely two of vuguguk, telidu and vamepek. I'll test vuguguk alone to learn more about the rule and about vuguguk.

TEST: vuguguk
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Only two rules fit all three results:
- **Any nexiom lights it:** vuguguk alone stayed dark, so it is not a nexiom. The nexioms must be telidu and vamepek.
- **It needs both nexioms:** vuguguk alone would stay dark either way. The nexioms could be any two of vuguguk, telidu and vamepek.

The other likely rules don't fit. "Exactly one nexiom" is ruled out because the two halves gave different results. "No nexioms" is ruled out because vuguguk alone would then have lit. "Not both" fails for the same reason.

So I'll test telidu and vamepek together:
- **If it lights:** telidu and vamepek are the nexioms under both rules.
- **If it stays dark:** the rule must be "needs both," and the pair is vuguguk with telidu or vuguguk with vamepek. My last test will tell those apart.

TEST: telidu, vamepek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

With telidu and vamepek dark together, the "any nexiom lights it" rule is ruled out, because under it those two would be the nexioms and would have lit.

To be thorough, I checked every rule that depends only on how many nexioms are on the machine (0, 1 or 2):
- **Split pairs are impossible.** If the nexioms were split between the two groups, each group would hold exactly one. One group lit and the other didn't, which is a contradiction.
- **So both nexioms are in {vuguguk, telidu, vamepek}.** The second group then had zero nexioms and stayed dark, so zero nexioms means dark.
- **Vuguguk must be a nexiom.** If it weren't, telidu and vamepek would be the pair and should have lit like the first group did. They didn't.
- **One nexiom means dark.** Vuguguk alone stayed dark.
- **The machine needs both nexioms.** The pair is either vuguguk + telidu or vuguguk + vamepek.

I'll test vuguguk with telidu. If it lights, those two are the nexioms. If it stays dark, the nexioms are vuguguk and vamepek.

TEST: vuguguk, telidu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Vuguguk and telidu together stayed dark, which rules out vuguguk + telidu as the pair. That leaves vuguguk and vamepek, which fit every result if the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it:
- **vuguguk, telidu, vamepek:** both nexioms, so it lit.
- **kaguku, lareges, buzekur:** no nexioms, so it stayed dark.
- **vuguguk alone:** one nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **telidu, vamepek:** one nexiom, so it stayed dark.
- **vuguguk, telidu:** one nexiom, so it stayed dark.

This conclusion assumes the machine depends only on how many nexioms are on it. I didn't test any other kind of rule.

ANSWER: nexioms = vuguguk, vamepek
One last question. If only vamepek were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No.** Telidu and vamepek together stayed dark. My answer says telidu is not a nexiom, and non-nexioms never affect the machine. So vamepek alone should behave exactly like telidu plus vamepek, which stayed dark.

This also fits the "needs both nexioms" rule: vamepek alone is just one nexiom, like vuguguk alone, which also stayed dark.

The first part rests only on telidu not being a nexiom. The second part relies on my answer and on the assumption that the machine depends only on how many nexioms are on it.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: gunape, rerulo, felurek, vezimek, pegefo, rumugun.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half the objects to see how the machine reacts.

TEST: gunape, rerulo, felurek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

That group didn't light it. Next I'll test the other three objects for comparison.

TEST: vezimek, pegefo, rumugun
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Testing one at a time would leave the rule unknown, so I'm working with possibilities.

- **Rules ruled out:** test 1 had no light and test 2 did. That rules out a rule where exactly one nexiom triggers the machine.
- **Rules still possible:** the machine lights if any nexiom is present, or only if both are present.
- **Where the nexioms are:** under either remaining rule, both must be among vezimek, pegefo and rumugun.

Testing vezimek alone helps separate these cases. If it lights, the "any nexiom" rule applies and vezimek is one of the pair.

TEST: vezimek
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The light pattern so far leaves two possible rules and three possible pairs.

- **"Lights if any nexiom is present":** test 1 clears gunape, rerulo and felurek, and test 3 clears vezimek. That leaves **pegefo + rumugun** as the only pair.
- **"Lights only if both are present":** both nexioms are among vezimek, pegefo and rumugun. The single-object test says nothing, so the pair could be vezimek + pegefo, vezimek + rumugun, or pegefo + rumugun.
- **Other rules:** "lights if no nexiom is present" and "lights unless both are present" would have made vezimek alone light up, so both are ruled out.

Next I'll test pegefo + rumugun together:
- **If it lights:** under either rule the pair must be pegefo + rumugun.
- **If it doesn't:** the pair is vezimek + pegefo or vezimek + rumugun, and one final test will separate them.

TEST: pegefo, rumugun
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Combining everything so far, the pair must be vezimek with either pegefo or rumugun.

- **Only one rule fits:** tests 1 and 2 together cover all six objects, so their nexiom counts add up to 2. One test lit and the other didn't, so the split was 0 + 2 or 2 + 0.
  - **Nexioms in gunape, rerulo, felurek:** the machine would light when no nexiom is present. Then vezimek alone should have lit, but it didn't, so this is ruled out.
  - **Nexioms in vezimek, pegefo, rumugun:** the machine lights with 2 nexioms and stays dark with 0.
- **Pair must include vezimek:** pegefo + rumugun didn't light. If they were the pair, it would have lit with 2 nexioms. So vezimek is a nexiom, and the machine stays dark with just 1. The rule is "lights only if both nexioms are present."
- **Final test:** I'll test vezimek + pegefo. If it lights, the pair is vezimek + pegefo. If not, it's vezimek + rumugun.

TEST: vezimek, pegefo
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The machine lit up with vezimek and pegefo together. That fits the rule that it lights only when both nexioms are present.

All five tests agree with this:
- **Test 1 (gunape, rerulo, felurek):** no nexioms, so no light.
- **Test 2 (vezimek, pegefo, rumugun):** both nexioms present, so it lit.
- **Test 3 (vezimek alone):** only one nexiom, so no light.
- **Test 4 (pegefo, rumugun):** only one nexiom, so no light.
- **Test 5 (vezimek, pegefo):** both nexioms present, so it lit.

ANSWER: nexioms = vezimek, pegefo
One last question. If only pegefo were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No, it would not light up. The tests show the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it together. pegefo is a nexiom, but alone it is only one of the two.

We have nearly seen this already. In test 4, pegefo was on with rumugun, which is not a nexiom and never affects the machine, and it stayed dark. Test 3 showed the same for vezimek alone. A single nexiom is not enough.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: refifes, finulir, takeker, dugase, daramo, zemeda.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by placing half the objects on the machine to see how it responds.

TEST: refifes, finulir, takeker
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three objects didn't light the machine. Next I'll test the other three to compare.

TEST: dugase, daramo, zemeda
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither half lit the machine, so a single nexiom alone is not enough. Two explanations fit so far:
- **Both needed:** the machine needs both nexioms, and they are split across the two halves (9 possible pairs).
- **Exactly one:** the machine lights only with exactly one nexiom, and both sit in the same half (6 possible pairs).

This test mixes two objects from the first group with one from the second. It should help separate those explanations and narrow down the pairs.

TEST: refifes, finulir, dugase
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three results leave six possible answers under two possible rules:
- **Both needed (AND):** one nexiom from each half, and both were in test 3. That gives refifes+dugase or finulir+dugase.
- **Exactly one (XOR):** both nexioms in the same half, with only one of them in test 3. That gives refifes+takeker, finulir+takeker, dugase+daramo or dugase+zemeda.

Two tests give at most four distinct outcomes, so I can't guarantee separating all six. I'll split them as evenly as I can.

This test should light up for refifes+dugase, refifes+takeker or dugase+zemeda. It should stay dark for finulir+dugase, finulir+takeker or dugase+daramo.

TEST: refifes, daramo, dugase
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Three candidates remain, and each one fits all four results so far:
- **finulir + dugase**, under the both-needed rule. Test 4 had no finulir, so it stayed dark.
- **finulir + takeker**, under the exactly-one rule. Test 4 had neither of them, so it stayed dark.
- **dugase + daramo**, under the exactly-one rule. Test 4 had both of them, so it stayed dark.

One test gives only two outcomes, so I can't guarantee separating all three. Testing takeker alone isolates one candidate:
- If it **lights up**, the answer is finulir + takeker.
- If it **stays dark**, it is finulir + dugase or dugase + daramo, and I'll have to pick one of the two.

TEST: takeker
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Takeker alone stayed dark, which rules out finulir + takeker. Two candidates are left, and both fit all five results:
- **finulir + dugase**, if the machine needs both nexioms.
- **dugase + daramo**, if the machine lights only with exactly one nexiom.

My tests can't tell these apart, so this is a 50/50 guess. I'll go with the both-needed explanation, since it seems the more natural rule for a detector.

ANSWER: nexioms = finulir, dugase
One last question. If only dugase were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Under my answer (finulir and dugase, both needed), **dugase alone would not light the machine**. Neither half lit up on its own, which fits the idea that one nexiom isn't enough.

This depends on my 50/50 guess, though. If the real answer is dugase and daramo under the exactly-one rule, dugase alone would light up. My tests couldn't separate those two cases. Testing dugase by itself would have settled it, but I had no tests left. I'm answering consistently with the answer I chose.

PROBE: no
